text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Sertraline started at 50 mg daily with a two-week tolerability check, and the dose adjusted by the PHQ-9
  • Weekly cognitive behavioral therapy for depression, with behavioral activation and work on self-reproach
  • PHQ-9 at every visit, structured safety assessment with a written safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, safety review at every visit, and a nurse phone check one week after starting
  • Neurology consultation to confirm the tic disorder, exclude other movement disorders, assess obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and advise on treatment
  • Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics (CBIT), eight sessions over ten weeks with a trained therapist, with psychoeducation for him and, if he wishes, his household
  • Tic severity measured with the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale at the consultation and at three and six months; tic medication held in reserve

resource.title: Samuel Johnson synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care for a 55-year-old writer with a severe recurrent major depressive episode and lifelong, never-diagnosed motor and vocal tics: measurement-based depression care with the PHQ-9, an SSRI with dose adjustment and psychotherapy, a structured safety assessment with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at every visit, recognizing adult Tourette syndrome and telling tics apart from chorea, assessing tic-related obsessive-compulsive symptoms, offering the Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics as initial treatment under the AAN guideline, and avoiding serotonergic and bleeding interactions when treating acute back pain in a patient on sertraline; built on the CMID depression monograph, the VA/DoD depression and suicide-risk guidelines, and the AAN 2019 tic guideline.
